title: Lazio Holds Under €2 a Litre While the Rest of Italy Tips Over
dek: Around Rome, self-service petrol is still a shade cheaper than the national line — even as a week-long upward drift keeps chipping away at the gap.
body: Drivers filling up in Lazio are paying €1.992 a litre for self-service Benzina and €2.105 for Gasolio as of August 17, both a notch below the national self-service averages of €2.005 and €2.124. That is a 1.3-cent cushion on petrol and a wider 1.8-cent gap on diesel — modest, but enough to keep Lazio just on the right side of the psychologically important €2 mark for Benzina, a line the national average has already crossed.

The relief is not new, but it is narrowing. Over the past week, self-service Benzina in the region has climbed from €1.983 to €1.992 and Gasolio from €2.086 to €2.105, a slow but steady creep upward every single day since August 11. Meanwhile the region's station network keeps expanding gently: 2,366 stations are now registered, up from 2,361 a month ago, with 2,107 reporting prices today — a reporting rate above 89% that suggests a healthy, actively monitored local market even as prices tick higher.

Pulling a same-day, region-by-region read like this out of a national dataset of over 93,000 price rows is exactly the kind of thing that used to live in a manually updated spreadsheet, refreshed whenever someone remembered. Fuel Dashboard instead rebuilds itself from the official MIMIT feed every day — built entirely with Claude Code — so a different region gets its own spotlight each morning without anyone touching a keyboard.
pull_quote: Lazio is still paying under €2 a litre for petrol — but the gap to the rest of Italy has been shrinking every day for a week.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Lazio, where self-service petrol is holding at €1.992/litre — still under the psychological €2 mark, and about 1.3 cents cheaper than the Italian national average.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating site that tracks petrol, diesel, LPG and methane prices across all of Italy's 20 regions, pulling directly from the official MIMIT government feed every single day. No manual data entry, no stale spreadsheet — just a live picture of where fuel is cheapest and how prices are moving, region by region.

The part I find genuinely useful to share: this entire pipeline — data ingestion, region selection, article writing, and the dashboard itself — is built and maintained with Claude Code. What used to be a manually updated Excel file is now a system that fetches, analyzes, and publishes itself daily. It's a small but concrete example of what AI-assisted development makes practical for a solo builder: a live analytics product with zero ongoing manual upkeep.

Check today's numbers and explore any region at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/
